decks.name: Bomb and survive
decks.note: Games where the bomb button is the whole strategy. Hold nothing back.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: Cave, in order
decks.note: Every Cave shooter the deck knows, oldest first. Watch the bullet patterns grow up.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: Danmaku in five steps
decks.note: One idea at a time: DonPachi teaches the laser, DoDonPachi the chain, Feveron speed, ESP Ra.De. bullet reading, Ketsui the lock-on. Play them in order.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: First hour on a tate cab
decks.note: Forgiving vertical shooters to learn the turned screen on. Nothing here punishes a first credit.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: Konami on a turned screen
decks.note: Konami turned its monitors the other way from everyone else. All four are clockwise; a cab set up for Cave needs the core's flip option.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: Learn to chain
decks.note: Cave's scoring in the order it was invented. Each game changes what a chain means, so the previous one is the lesson for the next.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: Psikyo, in order
decks.note: From Samurai Aces to Dragon Blaze. The bosses get bigger and the bullets get faster.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: The Raiden line
decks.note: Seibu's series in order, with Viper Phase 1 as the cousin in between. The plasma laser bends more every time.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: The Toaplan diaspora
decks.note: Batsugun was the last Toaplan game; its staff went on to make Raizing's. One lineage, one deck.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: Toaplan essentials
decks.note: The house that built the genre's spine. Tiger Heli to Batsugun.
decks.author: Lee Foot

decks.name: Two players
decks.note: Shooters that are better with someone beside you: shared bombs, shared scores, mutual blame.
decks.author: Lee Foot
